fields.statement: At commit 1b7da491 I ran go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(project-ls-rm|describe-golden|project-)' (ok), go test ./internal/rootcfg/... (ok), go test ./internal/api -run 'Project|Root' (ok), go vet and gofmt (clean). The project-ls-rm testscript registers a bare git checkout and an initialised one, sees 'not initialised' and 'initialised' in project ls and initialised false/true in project ls --json, runs project rm bare, finds bare/.git still on disk and bare gone from rhiza.toml and ls --json, and gets 'no project named bare' with a next: line for a second rm. I also ran a scratch build by hand in a hermetic root: ls --json lists name, path, initialised and repo (repo ID present for the initialised project); rm --dry-run left rhiza.toml unchanged; rm removed only [projects.bare] and kept the folder; a second rm exited 2 with next: rhiza project ls. I read the diff: rootcfg.Remove deletes only the map entry and rewrites the TOML file, and never touches project files.
